tech.about: Future tech base pack (FT1): technology is how far each limit on building things has been pushed. An advance moves a figure; the same sizing block still runs; past a figure's ceiling is fictional by arithmetic. Built by scripts/build-base-tech.py from the master data sheet.

sources.l3harris-rl10: L3Harris 2024, RL10 engine specification sheet: RL10B-2 specific impulse 465.5 s, thrust 24,750 lbf. https://l3harris.com/sites/default/files/2024-07/l3harris-ar-rl10-spec-sheet.pdf
sources.nasem2021: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2021, Space Nuclear Propulsion for Human Mars Exploration, chapter 2, Table 2.1: Rover/NERVA reactor tests, Pewee 1 about 875 s (vacuum, ideal expansion, from measured propellant temperature). https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/25977/chapter/4
sources.williams2005: Williams, C. H., Dudzinski, L. A., Borowski, S. K. and Juhasz, A. J. 2005, Realizing '2001: A Space Odyssey': piloted spherical torus nuclear fusion propulsion, NASA/TM-2005-213559 (AIAA 2001-3805): D-He3, specific impulse 35,435 s (Jupiter mission), jet power 4,830 MW, specific power 8.62 kW/kg
sources.adams2003: Adams, R. B. et al. 2003, Conceptual design of in-space vehicles for human exploration of the outer planets, AIAA 2003-4527 (NTRS 20030065984): D-He3 magnetised target fusion, specific impulse 77,000 s
sources.ball2019: Ball, J. 2019, Maximizing specific energy by breeding deuterium, arXiv:1908.00834, Table 1: D-He3 3.7 MeV per nucleon
sources.openstax-up3: Ling, S. J., Sanny, J. and Moebs, W. 2016, University Physics volume 3, OpenStax, section 10.5: fission of 1.00 kg of U-235 releases 8.21e13 J. https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-3/pages/10-5-fission
sources.pattarini2020: Pattarini, J. M. et al. 2020, Artemis sustained translational acceleration limits: human tolerance evidence from Apollo to ISS, NASA/TM-20205008196: seated, long duration, 4.91 m/s2 from 120 s on (head-to-foot axis)
sources.nasa-std-3001-v2: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2, requirement V2 6064, sustained translational acceleration limits, Tables 6.5-1 to 6.5-6 (tables not read)
sources.globus-hall2017: Globus, A. and Hall, T. 2017, Space settlement population rotation tolerance, NSS Space Settlement Journal: up to 4 rpm (56 m radius at 1 g) acceptable, up to 6 rpm for residents. https://nss.org/wp-content/uploads/NSS-JOURNAL-Space-Settlement-Population-Rotation-Tolerance.pdf
sources.nasa-iss-atcs: NASA and Boeing, International Space Station Active Thermal Control System overview: 70 kW rejected (35 kW per loop), ammonia supply 2.8 C. https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/473486main_iss_atcs_overview.pdf
sources.santarius-logan-1998: Santarius, J. F. and Logan, B. G. 1998, Generic magnetic fusion rocket model, Journal of Propulsion and Power 14, 519 (abstract read; full text not read)
sources.lubin2016: Lubin, P. 2016, A roadmap to interstellar flight, NASA NIAC phase I final report (NTRS 20190001185): a photon thrust of 3.3 nN per watt emitted
sources.nasa-std-3001-v1: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 revision C 2023, requirement V1 4030: career effective dose below 600 mSv. https://standards.nasa.gov/
sources.ochmo-tb-020: NASA OCHMO-TB-020 revision E 2022, radiation protection technical brief: at least 20 g/cm2 of shielding for missions longer than six months (solar particle events)
sources.koontz2016: Koontz, S. 2016, The International Space Station ionizing radiation environment, NASA JSC (NTRS 20160011221): median shielding 40 to 50 g/cm2 in the US Lab
sources.lynch2023: Lynch, C. et al. 2023, Logistics rates and assumptions for future human spaceflight missions beyond LEO, AIAA ASCEND 2023 (NTRS 20230013896): oxygen 0.89, drinking water 2.79, food as shipped 2.39 kg per crew member a day
sources.nasa-water2023: NASA 2023 (20 June), NASA achieves water recovery milestone on International Space Station: 98% total water recovery with the brine processor. https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/iss-research/nasa-achieves-water-recovery-milestone-on-international-space-station
sources.peng2008: Peng, B. et al. 2008, Nature Nanotechnology 3, 626: single carbon nanotube shells near 100 GPa (as summarised; not read)
